# Informed canonical Unit-map study

Copyright 2026 Masahiko G. Yamada. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0.

This is informed source authoring by Codex after reading the current source,
existing quantum-Unit study, primitive/type rules and the ordinary API decision
in Issue #43. It is not a blind-model benchmark. No external model was invoked;
the exact deployed model and sampling settings are unavailable.

The recorded next contract selects std::quantum::unit(ordinary Unit) -> Q<Unit>
and std::quantum::finish(Q<Unit>) -> ordinary Unit, with no static parameters,
Unitary effect and exact +1 coefficients. This ordinary source/API decision is
not a Guardian interpretation or guarantee admission. Q<Unit>, ordinary Unit,
and Q<Bits<0>> remain distinct. No implicit quantum elimination is requested.

All 22 complete schema-2, edition-2026 projects, their expected laws and this
context are preserved and hashed before any check. Desired sources use new
names known to be unimplemented in the baseline. A missing import or earlier
profile/parse error does not validate a downstream negative. Grouped negative
projects record several intended obligations but an actual first failure can
mask later declarations. None will be repaired in place.

Each project also has an empty observe main for finite-project checking. That
route checks declarations and the produced empty main; it does not execute an
open f or establish its phase. Selected checks target f. At most one system
qubit occurs in these programs; later independent semantic validation may use
a retained external reference. This baseline records diagnostics, not matrix
or reference-state experiments. No Rust/Lean build, corpus expansion, maximum
case, acceptance-rule change or general source-preservation theorem is claimed.

Separate-owner left/right wrappers preserve interface order but are not
packaged-tree unitors. The coherent packaged-tree example is explicitly a
separate sized-profile boundary. Pure finish must retain scalar multiplication;
measurement/discard cannot implement it. Observing argument evaluation must
remain even though the ordinary Unit value has no ports.
